daily_quests.title: ASX 200 Price Momentum with Window Functions
daily_quests.description: Using the ASX 200 historical prices dataset, write a query that calculates a 20-day rolling average price and identifies the rank of each stock by price momentum (percentage change from 20-day low to current price). Use window functions ROW_NUMBER() and LAG() to compute daily percentage changes, then rank stocks within each date partition. Filter for the top 10 momentum gainers on the most recent trading date. Expected output: stock symbol, current price, 20-day moving average, momentum rank, and percentage gain.

daily_quests.title: NSW Road Crash Data Cleaning and Risk Scoring
daily_quests.description: Download NSW Road Crash Data (Motor Accident data) from data.nsw.gov.au. Write a Python script using pandas to: (1) load and inspect the CSV for missing values and data types; (2) clean datetime columns and standardise suburb names (remove extra spaces, lowercase); (3) create a derived 'severity_score' column (1-5 scale) based on injury type and number of vehicles involved; (4) export the cleaned dataset to a new CSV with only complete rows. Expected output: cleaned CSV with at least 5000 rows, no null values in key columns, and a new severity_score column with values 1-5.
daily_quests.dataset: NSW Road Crash Data (Motor Accident data) — data.nsw.gov.au

daily_quests.title: Australian Weather Anomalies: Python ETL to SQL Analytics
daily_quests.description: Using Australian Weather observations dataset (from Bureau of Meteorology or Kaggle jsphyg collection): (1) Write a Python script to load daily temperature and rainfall CSV files, calculate monthly anomalies (deviation from 30-year average), and load cleaned data into a SQLite database with tables for 'stations', 'daily_observations', and 'monthly_anomalies'. (2) Write SQL queries to: identify the 5 stations with highest temperature anomalies in the past 12 months, rank months by rainfall deficit, and generate a summary view showing anomaly trends by state/territory. Expected output: SQLite database with 3 normalised tables, Python script handling data transformation, and 3 SQL queries producing ranked anomaly reports.
daily_quests.dataset: Australian Weather Observations — Bureau of Meteorology / Kaggle (jsphyg)
